$comment: Effect packs by Binbun (the owner bought the full editions). tools/content/prepare-vfx.mjs reads each Godot 4 pack (its scenes, materials and textures) and writes what the game draws: the effects' settings as JSON (`file`.json, from the pack's `dir`) and any pictures they sample, in packages/client/public/vfx (recorded in content/vfx.lock.json); only the effects `map` below names (and a pack's `keep`) are written. The packs themselves are never committed. `map` says which effect plays where; tools/content/vfx-map.mjs turns it into packages/client/src/game/fxMap.generated.ts (content:check fails when that is stale or names an effect that isn't shipped).

map.$comment: Effects by use. An effect is { pack, effect, scale } (pack: a pack's `file`, public/vfx/<file>.json: hit_fx, explosion_fx, electric_fx …). Lookups fall back from the most specific key to `default`.

muzzle.$comment: Muzzle flash by weapon family (WeaponDefinition.family; a weapon's own view.muzzle wins): effects of public/vfx/muzzle_flash.json. `projectile`: launchers with no family; `pellets`: other multi-pellet guns; `heavy`: other guns of 60+ damage.

impacts.$comment: A round hitting a surface, by surface type (content/surface-types.json, which says what each throws: dust, splinters, chips, leaves or sparks; its decal and sound family): the hole, sparks, dust and chips drawn in house (impactVisuals.ts) as set here, and an optional Binbun accent played on top (minor: dropped when many effects are playing, and past `accentRange` metres from the camera). `chips` are small lit flakes in `chip` colour: splinters on wood and bark, leaves on foliage, grit on rock.

weaponImpacts.$comment: Where a weapon's rounds land with their own effect, by weapon id or projectile visual (in place of the surface accent).

explosions.$comment: By weapon id first (the explode event's `w`), then its projectile visual, then the kind (barrel, trap, bomb, vehicle, air: a blast with no ground under it). Scale is per metre of blast radius.

gameplay.$comment: Moments of play: pickups (by item kind: pickup.<kind>), spawns, portals, jump pads, traps (trap.<type>) and ziplines. armor.break: sparks off a body whose armour a hit just broke. hit.big: a heavy hit landing on a body (both on the body's near side, half a metre toward the camera) (content/match-play.json heavyHit; scale per metre of the body's size). streak: a short burst over a player on a kill streak (3, 5, 10... kills in one life). Pickups, armor.break, hit.big and streak grow with distance past 3 m (up to 4 times, game/view.ts farSize), so they read across a room as they do 3 m off. `tint` (#rrggbb) recolours an effect (its secondary colour, the one Binbun's controllers set, and a pale wash of it on its white core). Minor effects: dropped when many effects are playing; with Reduce flashing on, armor.break, hit.big and streak play smaller and dimmer (game/view.ts).

arcs.$comment: Lightning (the `arc` event): a bolt laid along each jump (`zap`: its tube stretched to the jump, rooted where it lands; `width` scales its thickness; `speed` fits the pack's 0.6 s bolt to the game's 0.1-0.15 s between arcs) and a crackle where the last one lands (`hit`, minor). By who made it: an arc sentry (`mount`, in its violet), an electric fence (`fence`) or a gun (`default`: the Arc Caster).

lasting.$comment: Effects that last while something is so (started and stopped by the game; at most a few at once by graphics quality, the nearest first). charge.<mount>: an arc sentry winding up and holding its lock (scale per metre of its drawn charge ball). fire.zone: a burning patch (molotov, flamethrower, flare, lit oil; scale per metre of its radius, three or four overlapping). fire.vehicle / fire.wreck: a burning vehicle and the wreck smouldering (scale per metre of its size). fire.flare: a flare burning in flight or where it stuck. smoke.flare: the red smoke off an Airstrike Flare's shot, in flight and where it lands to mark the strike. fire.trap: a flame trap's jet (laid along it). cloud.toxic: a toxic gas cloud (scale per metre of its radius). smoke.wreck: the smoke column over a burning vehicle or its wreck (scale per metre of its size). shield.spawn: the faint shimmer round a player under spawn protection, until it drops (scale per metre of the body's size; Reduce flashing: a steady glow on the body instead). aura.damage / aura.speed: a low flame at the feet while a powerup is on (scale per metre of the body's size). flame.<kind>: the open flame of a fire prop (braziers, fire bowls, torches, candles, campfires): content/props.json gives each prop its flame point, size (scale per metre of flame height; the candle effect is half the fire's size, so torches and candles scale 2) and kind; `decor` ones come after every other lasting effect when places are handed out, and aren't drawn on low graphics. loot.<kind>: the glow on the floor under a pickup waiting to be taken (weapon, health, armor, ammo; Binbun's ground loot glows in the pack's gold, green and pale, armor tinted the game's blue), `decor` too: the nearest few pickups within 28 m, at most half the places, and with Reduce flashing on held still, dimmer and without sparkles (game/lootGlow.ts). `skip` leaves parts of an effect out (node names): here the pillars of light, which stood through the pickup itself, and the second rings and flares. portal: the swirl in a portal's frame while it is switched on (Binbun's Portal VFX, a gate; scale per metre of the portal's width over the pack's 2.5, its height fitted by the game; tinted the pair's colour by the game). pad: the column of light rising off a jump pad (Binbun's Magic Area VFX, the blue lift area). Both are `fixture`s: things of the map that matter to play, placed after the effects of the moment (fire, gas, a charge) and before every `decor` one (game/fixtureFx.ts). status.<kind>: the aura round another character that is burning, poisoned, slowed by goo, or chilled or frozen (Binbun's Stylized Status FX: flame, poison, rot tinted goo pink, ice; scale per metre of the body's size over the pack's 2 m figure; game/statusFx.ts picks the nearest few, never your own character, and slows and dims them with Reduce flashing on).
